project_catalog.standout_techniques: Measure->table->Douglas-Peucker knots->GSAP keyframes (knots: zoom 66, box 100, pan 62, glyph spin 25). Glyph spin settles exponentially at ~0.915 per 60 fps frame (tau ~0.19 s). Dive-into-glyph seam: the underscore becomes the input box. Split-flap: exit squash 1/.96/.85/.63/.28/0 about the cap line; entry 0->1 over 8-11 f from the baseline with a 4-8 px dip, per-slot stagger ~2 f, purple->black. Headline: cubic arc, tangent rotation +-16 deg, grey ghost 0.45 -> 1.45 overshoot lifted 55 px with +14 deg lean -> settle in ~10 f, onset ~2.8 f per glyph. Font chosen by per-glyph IoU (Heebo 900 0.891 vs Rubik 0.821). Renderer colour pre-compensation -3/-3/-4 (saturated), -3/-1/-1 (greys). Fidelity 14-frame MAD 2-10. Performer: generated still -> Veo 3.1 -> remove-background -> VP9 alpha WebM. Type: Inter 400/600 UI + Heebo 900 at 0.85 horizontal scale for the headline, white fill with a 3-layer black drop shadow. Camera: 2D wrapper #zoomg with transform-origin at the glyph centre; pan on #typed. Seams: none (continuous). Sound: none.

'No cuts and no crossfades between scenes' holds only for the four heygen-apple-motion templates. pr-to-video-launch uses eight 0.28-0.35 s power1.inOut crossfades; claude-paper/spacex a 0.6 s crossfade plus a hard cut at 6.7 s; HF-heygen-stripe a 0.3 s crossfade at 8.5 s and hard cuts at 27.0/32.25 s; figma-launch a 9-cut zoom ladder; hyperframes-launch hard smash cuts through its 14 s flex montage; k3-promo a two-frame inversion flash and a two-frame black dip; the frame-md render has 4 hard cuts. Restate as: morph or matched-surface hard cut; crossfade only when scenes do not share a ground (crossfade-dip law).

'One easing law, tau 0.131 s' is 02-bouncy-ui's default only (it also uses 0.135 for the flip and 0.168 for a growth). 01-ui-sting runs 1-2^(-10p) across each tween (median EO duration 1.01 s, tau ~0.146 s); 03-message-sting writes 1-2^(-10pD/T) with settle times T 0.12-0.53 s (tau ~0.017-0.076 s); 04-generate-reel uses power2/power3 + back.out(1.5); the paper-register films use cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) / expo.out 0.5 s. The shared law is exponential-out arrivals and mirrored exits; tau is chosen per move.

The zeta-1/3 three-channel spring (verified in 02-bouncy-ui/index.html L92-128, L474-480) is a register, not HeyGen's universal motion: the root README and 01-ui-sting say nothing overshoots, and claude-paper-launch/FRAME-claude.md bans tilt, spring and overshoot ('settle, never bounce'). 01 uses one decaying sine 19*exp(-t/0.279)*sin(2*pi*t/0.5) (2 Hz, zeta ~0.29) for a single element.

'No idle motion' is absolute only in the apple-motion templates and figma-launch. Other HeyGen films keep deliberate slow motion through holds: inspector-launch's halftone runs on a linear master tween that never stops ('should always be alive'); timeline-launch's act4 video drifts 1 -> 0.96 over 4.8 s after its entry; k3-promo's scene A pulls 1.07 -> 0.9417 over 3.667 s linear; HF-heygen-stripe's sunburst has a slow zoom/drift. Restate: no float/breathe/pulse on foreground objects; a slow linear camera drift continuing the entry vector, or a living background plate, is allowed.

The 'Motion after a cut: exponential-out' cell for HeyGen does not match the renders: after hard cuts motion rises (frame-md 1.0 -> 2.13 -> 2.57 at 100/200 ms; k3 1.0 -> 1.19 -> 1.71 -> 1.88 up to 400 ms) because HeyGen cuts to an empty or matched ground and starts the entrance after the cut.

The zoom-through row (1 -> 1.18 out, 0.92 -> 1 in) is template 03's version. The recipe reused across claude-paper, spacex, texture, inspector and frame-md is: out scale 1 -> 1.2 (or 0.8 inverse) + blur 20 px + opacity -> 0.15, power3.in 0.18-0.22 s; in from opacity 0.15, scale 0.75 (or 1.25), blur 20 px, expo.out 0.5 s. Video/card entries use 1.45 -> 1 with blur 14 -> 0 (0.62-0.9 s).

'Exits at 60-70% of the entrance duration' is a midpoint, not a rule: seam pairs in the corpus run 36-82% (zoom exits 0.18-0.22 s vs 0.5 s entries = 36-44%; cut-the-curve 0.11/0.16 = 69%, 0.14/0.19 = 74%, 0.22/0.32 = 69%, 0.45/0.55 = 82%); global medians power3.in 0.20 s vs power3.out 0.46 s, power2.in = power2.out = 0.26 s.

'GSAP's built-in expo.out is a different polynomial' is confirmed - the vendored GSAP 3.14.2 (k3-promo/assets/gsap.min.js) defines Expo easeIn as 2^(10(t-1))*t + t^6*(1-t) - but the difference from 1-2^(-10p) peaks at 0.78% of travel (p ~0.50). It matters for exact mirror symmetry and pixel replicas, not for feel.
The repo holds 20 project folders (23 films counting the four apple-motion templates separately, plus the hero compilation and two re-brand examples), not 'twenty-one launch compositions'.

'ledger.json - the seams' in the project shape: only the apple-motion templates (01, 04, the examples) ship ledger.json; the other films keep their seams in STORYBOARD/HANDOFF tables and code comments.
